description: Per-block inter-arrival thresholds (s) written by the unmodified ORACLES-tree IntArrAnalysis_time.m under GNU Octave, beside the port's intarr-threshold --blocks 5 output for the same proc file. Block = ceil(n/5) particles.

octave.command: octave-cli --no-gui, pkg load statistics optim netcdf, shim directory added to the path after the packages; driver run_iat_octave.sh, a development record

shims.+netcdf/open.m: supplies NC_NOWRITE when called with one argument (MATLAB's default; Octave's netcdf 1.0.20 requires the mode)
shims.histcounts.m: MATLAB edge semantics on histc, last edge inclusive (histcounts is not in Octave 11.3)
shims.plot and figure calls: no-op shims for bar, boxplot, colorbar, colormap, contourf, datetick, figure, gca, gcf, hold, legend, plot, print, set, title, xlabel, ylabel, ylim; none reaches threshhold_ak

octave.oracle_caveat: Octave's statset ignores the Robust and FunValCheck options, so Octave's nlinfit is a non-robust fit; agreement is agreement of two non-robust fits.

port.command: arrayprobe intarr-threshold --blocks 5 on the flight's HVPS proc file
port.files: HVPS_intArrThreshold_base<stem>.V_1.cdf, untracked (decoded output, not in the repository)

blocks.attribution: Fit difference in block 1 (hours 06-08); the slice-1 residual there is -1 particle, so it does not explain the flight's 0.43 % residual, which sits in blocks 2-5. May be the fitter (non-robust nlinfit), not the port.
